text: Atopic dermatitis has been defined by the American College of Veterinary Dermatology task force as “a genetically-predisposed inflammatory and pruritic allergic skin disease with characteristic clinical features” (Olivry, et al. Veterinary Immunology and Immunopathology 2001; 81: 143-146). The task force also recognized that the disease in canines has been associated with allergen-specific IgE (Olivry, et al. 2001 supra; Marsella & Olivry Clinics in Dermatology 2003; 21: 122-133). Severe pruritus, along with secondary alopecia and erythema, are the most noticeable and concerning symptoms to pet owners.
